title: Listen: the news and the first meeting with the Egyptian

blocks.text: This unit is dedicated to listening. In the first week you learn to listen to a simplified news: what to look for at first listening, how to take note of numbers and own names, what formulas come back every day ( ⁧وَفْقًا لِـ⁩ , ⁧أَعْلَنَ أَنَّ⁩ , ⁧أَشَارَ إِلَى أَنَّ⁩ , ⁧مِنَ المُتَوَقَّعِ أَنْ⁩ ). In the second week you meet for the first time the Egyptian Arab, the spoken variety that you heard on the street in Cairo. The goal is only to recognize it: to understand that a phrase is Egyptian, to identify the main traits (sounds, negation, future, present with ⁧بـ⁩ ) and bring it back to fuṣḥā. In this unit nothing is produced in dialect: you always speak and write in standard Arabic. Two weeks.

Egyptian scripts (D, E) are to be read by an Egyptian speaker (tutor, colleague, linguistic exchange): the vocal synthesis does not reliably pronounce the dialect. Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. use a strategy in three listenings (subject → data → details);
2. recognize the fixed formulas of the news and report a news with ⁧قَالَ إِنَّ⁩ , ⁧أَعْلَنَ أَنَّ⁩ , ⁧وَفْقًا لِـ⁩ ;
3. record numbers, dates, percentages and foreign names heard;
4. summarize a slow news in English;
5. recognizing the Egyptian: the sounds ( ⁧ج⁩ , ⁧ق⁩ , ⁧ث⁩ , ⁧ذ⁩ The present with ⁧بـ⁩ , the future ḥa- / ha-, denial But...-š and miš, the most frequent words;
6. Reaching a simple Egyptian phrase to fuṣḥā.

blocks.text: The verb-subject order. In the news the verb comes almost always first, and remains singular even with a plural subject: ⁧أُصِيبَ ثَلَاثَةُ أَشْخَاصٍ⁩ , ⁧اِجْتَمَعَ الوُزَرَاءُ⁩ . With ⁧قَالَ⁩ is used ⁧إِنَّ⁩ ( A2-19); with all other verbs ( ⁧أَعْلَنَ⁩ , ⁧أَشَارَ إِلَى⁩ , ⁧أَضَافَ⁩ , ⁧أَكَّدَ⁩ ) used ⁧أَنَّ⁩ .

The numbers are heard on the contrary. From 21 a 99 Arabic first says units: ⁧خَمْسَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ⁩ = 25 ('five and twenty'). When you listen, write the first digit to the right, or wait until the end of the number before writing. Years read in full (A2-12): ⁧عَامَ أَلْفَيْنِ وَسِتَّةٍ وَعِشْرِينَ⁩ In 2026», ⁧عَامَ أَلْفٍ وَتِسْعِمِئَةٍ وَثَمَانِيَةٍ وَثَمَانِينَ⁩ In 1988». Percentages end with ⁧بِالمِئَةِ⁩ ( A2-12). When you hear a name you don't know, write it in Arabic characters as you feel it, then try to rebuild the original. Countries and nationalities.
